name: Technitium DNS Server (Query Logs (Sqlite) app)
param_style: @name binds via Microsoft.Data.Sqlite AddWithValue (DateTime binds as TEXT 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.FFFFFFF'); the query-log WHERE clause is concatenated from the chosen filters at runtime
schema_source: Apps/QueryLogsSqliteApp/App.cs:420-526 (CREATE TABLE and the 13 CREATE INDEX statements InitializeAsync issues); only those statements are kept (GPL)
data_scale: scale 1: 250k dns_logs rows over 10 days (~135 MB with the app's 13 indexes), 120 clients (one client ~20 %), 8k distinct domains with a heavy head (top name ~10 %, top 40 ~25 %), ~14 % blocked, ~7 % NXDOMAIN; scale N multiplies rows (scale 4 = 1M rows, ~540 MB) and grows the domain tail by 2k per step
visibility_note: 10k stars; widely self-hosted recursive/authoritative DNS server (Pi-hole/AdGuard Home alternative); Query Logs (Sqlite) is the default query-log app offered in the App Store and the one the Logs > Query Logs tab uses out of the box
interest_note: One dynamic statement pair over a single wide table with 13 overlapping indexes (single-column, (timestamp,*), (client_ip,qname), (qname,qtype) and an 8-column index_all): the pager's Count(*) under every filter combination, ORDER BY dlid DESC LIMIT/OFFSET pages where the planner chooses between rowid walks and index scans plus sort, leading-wildcard LIKE, deep OFFSET CSV export, and the 15-minute retention count plus 10000-row batched DELETE.
reach_note: widely self-hosted DNS server; the SQLite query-log app is optional but the default way to get searchable query logs

cpu_evidence.summary: Query Logs (Sqlite) app 'gets really slow' with a 413 MB and a 4.2 GB querylogs.db; another user at 18 GB with 5-day retention; cleanup and full-log queries scale with table size
Query log page times out without a From/To range: the pager's SELECT Count(*) ... WHERE client_ip = ? took ~35 s (3.9M matches of 48M rows) in the MySQL sibling app, which issues the same SQL
40+ GB of query logs in SQLite; backup/restore and full-log handling impractical at that size

analyze_note: The app never runs ANALYZE (App.cs), so the planner works without sqlite_stat1.
